description: A double-underscore method (`__eq__`, `__add__`, `__repr__`) that built-in syntax and functions call on your object.
A value returned by a binary method to let Python try the reflected method of the other operand, and finally raise `TypeError`.
Objects that compare equal must have equal hashes. Defining `__eq__` alone sets `__hash__` to `None`.
A class decorator that fills in the missing comparison methods from `__eq__` and one ordering method.
`__radd__` and friends, called for `a + b` when `a` cannot handle `b`, as in `sum`'s `0 + first`.
